title: Ultra-Heavy Dark Matter Production in Active Galactic Nucleus Jets: A Falsifiable Multi-Messenger Framework
abstract: We investigate whether AGN jets can produce ultra-heavy dark matter (UHDM) with masses 10^15--10^19 eV through Standard Model particle collisions at center-of-mass energies sqrt(s) ~ 10^17--10^18 eV. Using GRMHD simulations, effective field theory parametrization, and multi-messenger observations (Fermi-LAT, IceCube, Pierre Auger), we predict production rates N_X ~ 10^10--10^15 s^-1 per AGN with factor-of-10^3 systematic uncertainties. Energy-loss-corrected calculations yield maximum particle Lorentz factors gamma_e,max ~ 10^6--10^7 (electrons) and gamma_p,max ~ 10^9--10^10 (protons), consistent with Fermi-LAT TeV observations and UHECR data. These energies lie within the EFT validity regime by nine orders of magnitude. Monte Carlo analysis scanning EFT couplings C_i = 10^-3--1 and jet parameters shows all predictions are consistent with Fermi-LAT, IceCube, and UHECR constraints. Integrating over AGN lifetimes and cosmic populations gives Omega_X^AGN ≲ 10^-10 Omega_DM---subdominant to primordial mechanisms but exhibiting unique spatial clustering and kinematic signatures testable by next-generation experiments (CTA, IceCube-Gen2, LISA).
